item.text: {"text":"BERT4Rec’s original generator uses overlapping windows, multiple random-mask copies, and one terminal-only masked copy per window; it does not uniformly sample users or all sequence prefixes. Random masking selects min(cap, max(1, round(length × rate))) targets, preventing zero-target examples for eligible nonempty sequences. Its trainer divides total target cross-entropy by total target count across the batch, rather than averaging each sequence’s mean loss. Consequently, examples with more targets receive greater batch weight; terminal-only examples have less weight than their frequency among examples suggests. Inference appends a reserved mask token and scores its representation. [Original generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py), [loss implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690).\n\nMathematically, sampling users uniformly and then one of each user’s K_u eligible endpoints gives endpoint probability 1/(U K_u); sampling uniformly over all eligible prefixes gives 1/ΣK_u and weights users proportionally to K_u. Eligibility must specify minimum context and inclusion of the final training interaction; excluding that endpoint removes its terminal supervision. Truncation changes context and interior-target exposure. For terminal-plus-interior training, define each example’s loss explicitly, e.g. λ·terminal CE + (1−λ)·mean interior CE; pooling all targets instead makes the terminal share depend on length and mask count. Independent Bernoulli masking has zero-target probability (1−p)^n: retaining such examples with zero loss downweights short histories, dropping/resampling them changes sampling probabilities, and forcing a target changes mask inclusion probabilities. These are derived consequences, not interchangeable implementations. With left padding, read the final nonpadding position; hide the terminal target and omit later interactions."}
